newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia govt says won't stack High Court.
newsitem.headline: Australia govt says won't stack High Court.

text.p: Australia's conservative government, facing another unexpected resignation from the High Court, said on Wednesday it would not seek to stack the country's peak court with conservatives.

The Liberal-National government, which has been critical of the court's progessive judgments, has the unusual opportunity to replace three of the court's seven judges within its first term after Justice John Toohey said he would quit two years early.
"What the government wants to do is to get the best people on the court for the job," Attorney-General Daryl Williams told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio.
"That will inevitably, no matter what is done, involve a mix of some kind."

The government must also replace the conservative Daryl Dawson, who retires earlier than expected in August, and chief judge Gerard Brennan, a moderate who will retire in May when he reaches the compulsory retirement age of 70.

Critics, including Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer, have said the court is dominated by progressive judges, appointed under the 13-year Labor government which was ousted last year, and favours flexible interpretations of the law in its rulings.

The critics have urged reform of the court and tighter controls on its operations after recent controversial decisions, including the December Wik judgment recognising Aboriginal land rights on pastoral land.
